chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the foundling (abandoned child). He (peace be upon him) said: 'She is neither to be sold nor bought, but employ her for whatever was spent upon her.'

key_terms.اسْتَخْدِمْهَا: Employ her / put her to work.
key_terms.بِمَا أَنْفَقْتَ عَلَيْهَا: For whatever was spent upon her (maintenance expenses).
key_terms.لَا تُبَاعُ: She is not to be sold.
key_terms.لَا تُشْتَرَى: She is not to be bought.
key_terms.لَّقِيطَة: Foundling; a child found abandoned without known parents.

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on buying, selling, and employing a foundling child?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the juristic status of a *laqitah* (foundling), ruling that she is not to be bought or sold as a slave but rather kept in service to offset the cost of her upkeep. This establishes a unique legal category distinct from chattel slavery, emphasizing stewardship and economic recovery over ownership. The ruling reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of balancing social welfare with property rights, ensuring the foundling is cared for without being commodified.
